name: Hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs)
summary: Anti-HBs is the antibody the immune system makes against the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Its presence at protective levels indicates immunity to hepatitis B, developed either after successful vaccination or after recovery from a past natural infection.
whatItMeans: A quantitative anti-HBs result reflects how much protective antibody is present. A concentration of at least 10 mIU/mL is generally considered protective (seroprotection), while a result below 10 mIU/mL is interpreted as not protected / non-immune and may prompt (re)vaccination in a susceptible person. When paired with a negative HBsAg and negative total anti-HBc, protective anti-HBs typically indicates vaccine-induced immunity; anti-HBs together with positive anti-HBc points to immunity from a resolved past infection. Antibody levels can wane over time, yet many vaccine responders retain immune memory and stay protected even when levels fall below 10 mIU/mL. This is educational information, not a diagnosis.
raises: Recovery from (resolved) natural hepatitis B infection
Booster or challenge dose of HepB vaccine in a prior responder
Recent hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) administration (passive antibody)
lowers: Waning of vaccine-induced antibody over the years
Non-response or poor response to the vaccine series
Immunosuppression (e.g. dialysis, HIV, immunosuppressive therapy) blunting the antibody response
Older age or obesity reducing vaccine response
confounders: Assay-to-assay variability; results near the 10 mIU/mL cutoff can differ between labs
Recent HBIG or blood-product administration gives passively acquired anti-HBs that is not vaccine- or infection-derived
Timing matters: post-vaccination testing is standard at 1–2 months after the final dose
Very high or very low values may be reported as out-of-range rather than an exact number
A qualitative (positive/negative) result cannot distinguish borderline from robustly protective titers

ranges.note: ≥10 mIU/mL is the standard threshold for seroprotection/immunity (CDC/WHO). <10 mIU/mL is interpreted as not protected / non-immune (susceptible). Some labs report ~100+ mIU/mL as robust immunity. Cutoffs are assay-dependent; interpret with HBsAg and anti-HBc. Educational/typical values only.
